photos.question: A client is starting ciprofloxacin for a urinary tract infection. Which adverse effect should the client report right away?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #266!

💊 One common antibiotic has a warning about a very specific body part. Do you know it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Pain or swelling in the heel

🧠 Rationale: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic.

These drugs carry a boxed warning for tendinitis and tendon rupture, most often the Achilles tendon.

Heel pain or swelling means stop exercise and call the provider right away.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Ciprofloxacin

💊 Drug Class: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic

❤️ Primary Use: UTIs and other bacterial infections

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Tendon pain or rupture

🔹 Nausea and diarrhea

🔹 Sun sensitivity

🔹 Dizziness

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Report heel or tendon pain right away

✅ Drink plenty of fluids

✅ Take 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids, iron or calcium

✅ Use sunscreen

🚑 Higher Risk: Older adults, steroid use, kidney, heart or lung transplant

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Cipro? Protect the heel you go!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Pharmacology #Antibiotics #Fluoroquinolones #NursingPharm #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse teaches a client with heart failure about a low-sodium diet. Which statement shows understanding?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #267!

🧂 Salt hides in more foods than most clients think. Which answer shows real understanding?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — "I will avoid canned and processed foods."

🧠 Rationale: Sodium makes the body hold on to fluid.

In heart failure, extra fluid strains the heart and causes swelling and shortness of breath.

Canned soups, deli meats, soy sauce and processed foods are some of the biggest sodium sources.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Heart Failure Diet

❤️ Why It Matters: Less sodium means less fluid overload

⚠️ High-Sodium Foods:

🔹 Canned soups and vegetables

🔹 Deli and cured meats

🔹 Soy sauce and pickles

🔹 Frozen and fast foods

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Read food labels for sodium

✅ Choose fresh foods and season with herbs

✅ Weigh daily at the same time

🚑 Call the Provider: Gain of 2 to 3 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Fresh is best, cans are a salt test!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #HeartFailure #CardiacNursing #LowSodium #PatientTeaching #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Which hemoglobin A1C result meets the criterion for a diagnosis of diabetes?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #268!

🩸 One lab value tells you about the last 3 months of blood sugar. Do you know the cutoff?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — 6.8%

🧠 Rationale: An A1C of 6.5% or higher meets the criterion for diabetes.

5.7% to 6.4% is prediabetes, and below 5.7% is normal.

Only 6.8% is at or above 6.5%.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Hemoglobin A1C

🩸 What It Shows: Average blood glucose over about 3 months

📊 Ranges:

🔹 Normal: below 5.7%

🔹 Prediabetes: 5.7% to 6.4%

🔹 Diabetes: 6.5% or higher

🎯 Common Goal: Below 7% for many adults with diabetes

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ No fasting needed for this test

✅ Usually checked every 3 to 6 months

✅ Teach that it reflects long-term control

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

6.5 and up, diabetes shows up!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Diabetes #Endocrine #A1C #NursingLabs #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client was hit in the head during a fall. Which finding suggests a basilar skull fracture?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #269!

🧠 One bruise in a very specific spot is a big NCLEX clue. Can you spot it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD neuro question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Bruising behind the ears

🧠 Rationale: Bruising behind the ears over the mastoid bone is called Battle sign.

It is a classic sign of a basilar skull fracture.

Bruising around both eyes (raccoon eyes) and clear fluid from the nose or ears are other signs.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Basilar Skull Fracture

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Battle sign: bruising behind the ears

🔹 Raccoon eyes

🔹 Clear fluid from the nose or ears

🔹 Halo sign on gauze

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Do not insert an NG tube through the nose

✅ Do not suction through the nose

✅ Tell the client not to blow the nose

✅ Check fluid for glucose (CSF)

🚑 Watch For: Meningitis and rising ICP

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Battle behind the ears, raccoon around the eyes!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #NeuroNursing #HeadInjury #SkullFracture #TraumaNursing #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse notes continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber of a client's chest tube system. What does this indicate?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #270!

🫁 Bubbles in a chest tube can be normal or a problem. Do you know which chamber matters?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — An air leak in the system

🧠 Rationale: Continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber means an air leak.

Gentle bubbling in the suction control chamber is expected with wet suction.

Intermittent bubbling in the water seal with coughing or exhaling can be normal with a pneumothorax.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Chest Tubes

🫁 Water Seal Chamber:

🔹 Tidaling up and down with breathing is normal

🔹 Continuous bubbling means an air leak

🔹 Tidaling stops when the lung re-expands or the tube kinks

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check connections from the client to the drain

✅ Keep the drain below the chest

✅ Keep the tubing free of kinks and loops

✅ Never clamp without an order

🚑 Report: Sudden drainage over 100 mL/hr or new trouble breathing

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Water seal bubbling nonstop? Look for the leak!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #ChestTube #RespiratoryNursing #MedSurg #ICUNursing #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client at 30 weeks of pregnancy feels dizzy and lightheaded while lying flat on her back. What should the nurse do first?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #271!

🤰 Lying flat can cause trouble late in pregnancy. What is the quick fix?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Turn the client onto her left side

🧠 Rationale: Lying flat lets the heavy uterus press on the inferior vena cava.

Less blood returns to the heart, so blood pressure drops and the client feels dizzy.

Turning to the left side takes pressure off the vena cava and restores blood flow.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Supine Hypotensive Syndrome

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Dizziness and lightheadedness

🔹 Pale, clammy skin

🔹 Low blood pressure

🔹 Fast heart rate

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Turn to the left side

✅ Use a wedge under the right hip if the client must be on her back

✅ Recheck vital signs

✅ Monitor the fetal heart rate

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Feeling faint? Go left, it's great!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Maternity #OBNursing #Pregnancy #MaternalHealth #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse teaches a client with GERD. Which instruction should the nurse include?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #272!

🔥 Heartburn every night? One simple habit makes a big difference. Do you know it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD GI question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Avoid lying down for 3 hours after eating

🧠 Rationale: Staying upright for 2 to 3 hours after eating keeps acid in the stomach.

Large meals and lying down after eating increase reflux.

Peppermint, chocolate, caffeine and fatty foods relax the lower esophageal sphincter.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: GERD

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Heartburn after meals

🔹 Sour taste or regurgitation

🔹 Chronic cough or hoarse voice

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Eat small, frequent meals

✅ Raise the head of the bed 6 to 8 inches

✅ Avoid caffeine, chocolate, peppermint and fatty foods

✅ Stop smoking and limit alcohol

💊 Common Meds: Antacids, H2 blockers, proton pump inhibitors

🚑 Report: Trouble swallowing, vomiting blood or black stools

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Stay up after you sup!
